name: John Frederick Kensett
summary:
John Frederick Kensett was an American
landscape painter and engraver born in Cheshire, Connecticut. He was a member of the second generation of the Hudson River School of artists. Kensett's signature works are landscape paintings of New England and New York State, whose clear light and serene surfaces celebrate transcendental qualities of nature, and are associated with Luminism.

Kensett's early work owed much to the influence of Thomas Cole, but was from the outset distinguished by a preference for cooler colors and an interest in less dramatic topography, favoring restraint in both palette and composition. historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Kensett's landscape paintings of New England and New York State helped define the Luminist movement, a regional art style that celebrated the beauty of nature. His work influenced American artists for generations to come.
